🔬 **Apple Scab** (Venturia inaequalis)
**Plant:** Apple

**Symptoms:**
• Olive-green, velvety spots appearing on the top and bottom of leaves.
• Leaves twist, pucker, and turn yellow, resulting in early leaf drop.
• Apples show corky, scabby brown lesions that crack as they expand, distorting fruit shape.

**Causes:**
Venturia inaequalis fungus. Overwinters on fallen dead leaves. Spores are released by spring rains and blown by wind onto new leaves.

**Treatment:**
✔ Apply organic sulfur or copper fungicides starting from green tip stage in spring through petal fall.
✔ Remove scabby fruit from the tree early to focus tree energy on healthy fruit.
✔ Apply agricultural lime to fallen leaves in autumn to accelerate leaf decomposition.

**Prevention:**
🛡️ Rake and destroy all fallen leaves in autumn to eliminate overwintering spores.
🛡️ Plant scab-resistant cultivars (e.g., Honeycrisp, Liberty, Enterprise).
🛡️ Prune branches to open up the canopy, letting leaves dry quickly after rains.

⚠️ For accurate diagnosis, please also consult a local agricultural expert.

**Disease Detected:** Leaf Scorch
**Plant Type:** Strawberry
**Confidence:** 87.6%
**Method:** 🔍 Detected using image analysis

🔬 **Leaf Scorch** (Diplocarpon earlianum)
**Plant:** Strawberry

**Symptoms:**
• Numerous small, irregular, dark purple to red spots scattered across the upper leaf surface.
• Spots enlarge and their centers turn grayish-brown while margins remain dark purple.
• Severely infected leaves appear 'scorched', curl upward, and drop prematurely.

**Causes:**
Diplocarpon earlianum fungus. Overwinters in infected leaf tissue and crowns. Wet, rainy spring weather triggers mass spore release.

**Treatment:**
✔ Apply captan, thiram, or myclobutanil fungicides at 7–10 day intervals during wet spring seasons.
✔ Renovate strawberry beds after harvest by mowing and removing old foliage.
✔ Mulch beds with straw to reduce soil splash that spreads fungal spores.

**Prevention:**
🛡️ Remove and destroy all old leaf debris before new growth emerges each spring.
🛡️ Avoid overhead watering; use drip irrigation to keep leaves dry.
🛡️ Space strawberry plants adequately (12–18 inches apart) for good air circulation.

⚠️ For accurate diagnosis, please also consult a local agricultural expert.
